title: Evaluation of an encoded gate list
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $R$ be a finite bit string, let $P$ be a finite list of finite bit strings, and let $gs$ be a finite list of arithmetic gates with input variables among $n$ variables. Assume that each gate at position $i$ that is an addition, subtraction, or multiplication refers only to gate positions strictly less than $i$. Put $m=\mathrm{val}(R)+1$, and assign input variable $j$ the value $\mathrm{val}(P_j)+1$, taking the value to be $0$ when $j$ is beyond the end of $P$. Then running the gate evaluator on the encoding of $gs$, paired with the context determined by $n$, $R$, and $P$, produces the state encoding with that same context, terminal word $[0]$, and the list of gate values evaluated successively modulo $m$, starting from the empty list of prior values.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite list of finite bit strings
$gs$ is a finite list of arithmetic gates on $n$ inputs
Every addition, subtraction, or multiplication gate at position $i$ refers only to positions strictly less than $i$
